AFF 2024-2026 African Forest Ecosystems Support (PHASE II Transition)

description.narrative: Insatsen har två mål: Den ska omforma AFF till att ha en förbättrad kapacitet att verka för bättre levnadsvillkor och hållbar miljö genom en bättre styrning av Afrikas skog och trädresurser och därigenom bidra till en ökad biologisk mångfald, bättre levnadsvillkor och en ökad stabilitet kontinentalt. Dess andra mål är att AFF har uppnått finansiell säkerhet utan Sidas stöd och att AFF kan bidra till en hållbar skog­ och landskapsstyrning i Afrikas länder.

The intervention has a two­fold objective; firstly it aims to transform the African Forest Forum to enhance its capacity to improve livelihoods and environmental stability through better management of African Forest and Tree resources and further to achieve improved management of forest and tree resources for biodiversity conservation, livelihood and stability in Africa. Second goal is that AFF has achieved financial security and supports African countries to achieve sustainable forest and landscape management.

The intervention has a two-fold objective;
The first goal is to enhance African Forest Forum's capacity to improve livelihoods and environmental stability through better management of African Forest and Tree resources and further to achieve improved management of forest and tree resources for biodiversity conservation, livelihood and stability in Africa.
The second goal is that AFF has achieved financial security and supports African countries to achieve sustainable forest and landscape management. This will be achieved by four components:
Component 1: Improved social and biophysical resilience through better management and conservation of forest biodiversity.
Component 2: Sustaining renewable energy in forest biodiversity hotspots.
Component 3: Strengthening AFF´s capacity and partnership opportunities for creation and knowledge sharing for improved evidence based decision making
Component 4: Transforming AFF for sustainability.

In 2024, the African Forest Forum (AFF) Secretariat made significant progress in advancing its transformation agenda by initiating expert recruitment and implementing project activities aligned with four key components. Under Component 1: Biodiversity Management and Conservation, the AFF aimed to improve forest biodiversity management for ecosystem and human well-being. Key milestones included the development of Terms of Reference (ToRs) for three analytical studies, contracting eight experts across five biodiversity hotspots, initiating methodology harmonization, and producing four inception reports.
Component 2 focused on promoting renewable energy in forest biodiversity hotspots by assessing sustainable tree-based energy options. ToRs were developed for a major study scheduled for advertisement in 2025, and plans are in place to recruit seven national experts in the first quarter of that year. Component 3: Knowledge Management and Information Sharing emphasized improving communication and awareness. Key achievements included maintaining the AFF portal with extensive database and partner links, expanding knowledge products, piloting grassroots projects in East Africa, engaging regional media experts, and establishing a monitoring system and policy interface, including Africas Common Position for UNFF19.
Finally, Component 4: Transforming AFF for Sustainability targeted institutional longevity and impact. Major actions included initiating a governance review, defining a new programmatic approach with four thematic areas, and increasing AFFs visibility through global participation and co-hosting events. Additionally, the Secretariat secured nearly USD 800,000 in funding, submitted 11 new proposals, and expanded outreach with a strong global digital presence. Staff capacity building also progressed with training sessions and internships, while discussions began on a potential membership fee system to ensure long-term sustainability.
